# Secondary Cast — Design Rules and Exemplars

## Design rules

> status: ratified (D-0033, D-0034, D-0075)

Every secondary character is a living consequence of the system, never an NPC. Bad
people are bad because of incentives; there is a wide range of grays; people do bad
things to avoid starving. Working-class complicity is shown honestly — the miner who
defends the mine, the elder who informs on strangers — without contempt. And the
secondary cast carries what the core trio cannot: romance, desire, marriages,
flirtation — the world's stubborn warmth ([[womens-lives]]).

## Proposed exemplars

> status: proposed

Session sketches, names unratified (Q-0015 — note the "Silas" double-booking with a
cold-open example):

- **The debt-widow ("Oona")** — drowned-lowlands bog-harvester living outside the
  rolls since her husband's debts transferred to her. Not a weeping victim: flinty,
  suspicious, and fluent in the gift-debt economy — her offered stew is a contract
  ([[economy]]).
- **The checkpoint bailiff ("Silas")** — lower-chalk functionary with stained hems
  and an abacus; enforces quotas he privately doubts because his daughter's place in
  the keep depends on it. His scenes play as drawing-room terror, out-bureaucratized
  rather than out-fought.
- **The cunning-man ("Kaelen")** — crag-country amulet-peddler selling fakes to
  frightened miners while hiding his real inherited craft, because demonstrated
  competence gets you conscripted. Contempt from the protagonist, understanding
  eventually from the apprentice: hiding your gift is also survival.
- **The smuggler couple ("Cerys & Jorin")** — salt-fringe river-runners working the
  scrip-exchange rackets; young, in love, financially irrational about it — the
  jar-of-honey-for-a-blue-bead people. They teach the apprentice that the ledger's
  math is not the only math.
- **The blind midwife** — a hunted folk-saint carrying birth-rites camp to camp
  ([[religion]]); the compromised local scholar informing for medicine; the cowardly
  keep-clerk who wants to leak and can't quite — the recurring middle-gray gallery.
